_about: LAC (LCD Alarm Clock): where the wires run in the CAD and how the breadboard is laid out, measured from lac.glb (converted from LAC Full Build.STEP) on 19 Oct 2026 by docs/research/lac/scripts (wires3.py, poses.py, make_wire_paths.py). Millimetres in assembly space, Y up, as assembled. 'lines': the centre line of every wire body the CAD has (they are left out of the model: the player draws the wires), with the Dupont cap nearest each end ('cap_a' / 'cap_b', distance in mm: 0 = the line ends inside that cap) and its colour in TechBox's published LAC Cadasio project. 'caps': every Dupont cap (male 'Wire Cap V2': a 1.75 mm square housing 8 mm long over an 8 mm pin, 4 mm of it below the housing; female 'Wire Cap', the MRA's part); for a male cap standing in the breadboard, 'top' (the housing's top, where the wire leaves it), 'wire_at' (where the CAD's wire ends, inside the housing) and 'tip'. 'holes': every terminal hole's top (a1 ... j30; rows a - e and f - j, columns 1 - 30 along -z), fitted to the caps the CAD has in them; the power rails are 'rails'. 'poses': the CAD's posed copies of a part relative to its seated copy (stepgen poses: [x, y, z] or {t, r, at}).

breadboard.rail_note: rail holes lie at z = 1284.92 + 2.54 k (in groups of five), half a pitch from the terminal columns: a lead from a rail to a terminal hole does not run square to the board
breadboard.unused_rails: the two rails on the j side, about x 651.0 and 653.5
